The Relative Strength Index is a widely used momentum indicator that measures the speed and magnitude of recent price movements on a scale of 0 to 100. Readings above 70 typically suggest that a stock has entered overbought territory following a sustained advance, while readings below 30 indicate oversold conditions. The indicator is generally calculated using a 14-day lookback period.

Although an elevated RSI does not necessarily signal an imminent reversal, investors often monitor these stocks during earnings season, when quarterly results and management guidance can reinforce positive sentiment or trigger profit-taking.
